lead: In Part 4 one person speaks: an announcement, a voicemail, a tour, an advertisement or a speech. Topic questions ask what the talk is about, why the speaker is calling, or who the speaker and the listeners are.
第 4 部分由一個人說話：公告、語音留言、導覽、廣告或演說。主旨題問談話的主題、說話者為什麼來電，或說話者與聽眾是誰。
steps: Read the questions first, when there is time, so you know what to listen for.
有時間的話先看題目，知道該聽什麼。
Identify the type of talk from the opening: 'Attention, passengers', 'Thank you for calling', 'Welcome to'.
從開頭判斷談話類型：Attention, passengers、Thank you for calling、Welcome to。
Catch the topic in the first sentences. The rest of the talk supports it.
在前幾句抓到主題，其餘內容是在支持它。
Choose the option that covers the whole talk, not one detail.
選涵蓋整段談話的選項，不是單一細節。

head: The opening names the type and the speaker
開頭點出類型與說話者
body: Standard openings tell you what kind of talk it is and who is speaking or listening. Listen for these before the details start.
固定的開場白會告訴你談話類型，以及誰在說、誰在聽。在細節開始前先抓住它們。
ex: Thank you for calling Westfield Dental. Our office is closed today. (a clinic's recorded message)
感謝來電 Westfield 牙科。本診所今天休診。（診所的錄音訊息）
Attention, passengers on Flight 82. Boarding will begin shortly. (an airport announcement)
82 號班機的旅客請注意，即將開始登機。（機場廣播）

head: The topic comes early, details support it
主題在前，細節在後
body: The first sentences often say what the talk is about. Later sentences add times, places and instructions. Hold on to the first idea.
前幾句常會說明談話的主題，之後才補上時間、地點和指示。記住最先出現的那個想法。
ex: This is an update on parking. From Monday, Lot B will be closed. Topic: parking changes.
這是停車的最新消息。星期一起 B 停車場關閉。主旨：停車場異動。

head: Purpose phrases
表示目的的說法
body: Listen for phrases that state the purpose: 'I'm calling to', 'I'd like to remind you', 'I'm pleased to announce', 'I want to thank'.
留意直接說明目的的片語：I'm calling to、I'd like to remind you、I'm pleased to announce、I want to thank。
ex: I'm calling to let you know your order is ready for pickup.
我來電是要通知您，訂單已可取貨。
I'd like to remind you that timesheets are due on Friday.
提醒各位，工時表星期五截止。

head: Details are not the topic
細節不是主旨
body: An option that matches one time, place or name is often too narrow. Ask whether it covers the whole talk.
只符合一個時間、地點或名字的選項常常範圍太小。要問它是否涵蓋整段談話。
ex: Talk: road work, a delay and detours. Topic: a construction schedule. 'The detour map' is a detail.
談話：道路施工、延誤、改道。主旨：施工時程。「改道地圖」是細節。

head: Speaker and audience from word choice
從用字判斷說話者與聽眾
body: Words such as 'your boarding pass', 'our new hires' and 'shoppers' show who is listening. The speaker's job comes from what is offered or explained.
your boarding pass、our new hires、shoppers 這類字顯示聽眾是誰。說話者的職業則由他提供或說明的內容判斷。
ex: 'Please keep your boarding passes ready.' = travelers at an airport.
「請準備好您的登機證。」＝機場的旅客。

head: Options reword the topic
選項會改寫主題
body: The talk says 'we're running late'. The option says 'a delay'. Match the meaning of the whole message.
談話說 we're running late，選項寫 a delay。要比對整段訊息的意思。
ex: 'The store will be closed for inventory.' = a temporary closure.
「本店因盤點暫停營業。」＝暫時休業。

pairs.right: Q: What is the announcement mainly about? [Man: Starting Monday, the staff cafeteria closes for painting. Please use the café across the street.] / A: A temporary cafeteria closure.
pairs.wrong: Q: What is the announcement mainly about? [Man: Starting Monday, the staff cafeteria closes for painting. Please use the café across the street.] / A: The hours of a nearby café.
why: The café is only the alternative. The main message is that the cafeteria is closing.
對面的咖啡館只是替代方案，主要訊息是員工餐廳要關閉。

pairs.right: Q: Why is the speaker calling? [Man: This is Ben from Delta Print. Your business cards are ready for pickup.] / A: To say an order is ready.
pairs.wrong: Q: Why is the speaker calling? [Man: This is Ben from Delta Print. Your business cards are ready for pickup.] / A: To ask for payment.
why: Payment is never mentioned. The call is to say the order can be picked up.
沒有提到付款。這通電話是通知訂單可以取貨。

pairs.right: Q: Who is the speaker? [Man: Good morning, class. Please open your textbooks to page ten. Today we'll practice writing business e-mails.] / A: An instructor.
pairs.wrong: Q: Who is the speaker? [Man: Good morning, class. Please open your textbooks to page ten. Today we'll practice writing business e-mails.] / A: A bookstore clerk.
why: 'Textbooks' pulls toward a bookstore, but 'class' and 'we'll practice' name the role.
textbooks 讓人想到書店，但 class 和 we'll practice 才點出身分。

head: Typical question wordings
常見問法
items: What is the announcement mainly about?
這則公告主要在談什麼？
What is the purpose of the message?
這則留言的目的是什麼？
What is the talk mainly about?
這段談話主要在談什麼？
Who most likely are the listeners?
Where is the announcement most likely being made?
這則公告最可能在哪裡發布？

traps: Choosing a detail. A time, a place or a name from the talk is not its topic. Ask whether the option covers the whole message.
選了細節。談話中的時間、地點或名字不是主題。要問選項是否涵蓋整段訊息。
Being misled by the first words. Greetings and thanks come before the point. The topic often starts after them.
被開頭的話誤導。問候和道謝在重點之前，主題常在它們之後才開始。
Using background knowledge instead of the audio. Choose what the speaker says, not what such a talk usually contains.
用背景知識取代音檔。要選說話者實際說的，而不是這類談話通常會有的內容。
An option that repeats words from the talk but changes the meaning. Compare the idea, not the vocabulary.
選項重複談話的字，意思卻變了。要比對想法，而不是詞彙。
